From which source does the live verification's plugin-install check add the marketplace and install the plugin?

The goal lists the `uHappyLogic/cairn-codex` distribution repository as part of the release-ready surface, while the release skill's pre-flight already stops on a missing repository and prints the `gh repo create` and `gh repo edit` commands, and the traffic-token step is deferred to the first Codex release. Is the empty `uHappyLogic/cairn-codex` repository created inside this milestone, or left to the maintainer at the first Codex release?
open-question.alternative: The empty `uHappyLogic/cairn-codex` repository is created during this milestone by the maintainer, by hand. The maintainer runs the same two commands the release skill's step 2f prints: a public `gh repo create` with the fixed description and no license, README or gitignore, then `gh repo edit` to add the `cairn`, `codex` and `plugin` topics and disable issues, wiki and projects. The milestone's task list holds a task that stops until the repository exists and then records a read-only `gh repo view` read-back of its existence and settings in `TASKS_DONE.md`. No content is pushed and the `TRAFFIC_TOKEN` secret is not set, so the first publish is still the root commit at the first Codex release. It meets the goal's wording literally, because the distribution repository it lists as part of the release-ready surface exists when the milestone ends. It also follows milestone 23, where the maintainer created both existing distribution repositories inside the milestone that introduced them, and it reserves the `cairn-codex` name now. It does not save the first Codex release a stop. The recorded Traffic token extension decision defers the token step to that release and adds a pre-flight stop on the missing secret, so that run stops anyway. Until that release, a public, empty repository is visible with nothing in it. The manual step also breaks a headless run of the task list, because the runner has to wait for the maintainer.

The empty `uHappyLogic/cairn-codex` repository is created during this milestone by the task runner, not by hand. A task in the milestone runs the release skill's two step-2f commands with the already-authenticated `gh`: a public, deliberately empty `gh repo create` with the fixed description, then `gh repo edit` for the topics and to disable issues, wiki and projects. The same task reads the result back with `gh repo view` and records it in `TASKS_DONE.md`. No content is pushed and the `TRAFFIC_TOKEN` secret is not set. It is the only way to have the repository exist at milestone end with no handoff to the maintainer. The task list stays fully automatable and headless, and the read-back of the settings becomes part of the recorded evidence. An agent would perform a public act that cannot be undone, and both milestone 23 and the release skill reserve that act to the maintainer. The release skill says of these same commands that the skill must never run them. As with the maintainer option, the first Codex release still stops on the missing `TRAFFIC_TOKEN` secret, and an empty public repository sits visible until then.

The repository is not created in this milestone and the task list has no task for it. At the first Codex release, the release skill's existing step-2f pre-flight finds `uHappyLogic/cairn-codex` missing, stops, and prints the `gh repo create` and `gh repo edit` commands. The maintainer runs them then. At that same release, the maintainer also extends the `TRAFFIC_TOKEN` as the recorded Traffic token extension decision describes. The goal's mention of the repository is met by the release path already handling it, not by the repository existing. It adds no work and no new mechanism, because the host-agnostic pre-flight already covers a missing repository by design. It also puts all one-time provisioning for the new host at one moment, the first Codex release. That is where the token step already sits, and the token cannot be extended to a repository that does not yet exist. The goal names the `uHappyLogic/cairn-codex` repository among the release-ready surface, so this reading leaves that item unbuilt when the milestone ends. It holds only if "release-ready" means the release path is ready. Otherwise the goal needs an edit through `modify-milestone-goal`. Until the release, the install route documented on `main` names a repository that does not exist. The first Codex release also stops at least once at pre-flight and has to be re-run after the maintainer acts.

`docs/ways-of-using-cairn.md` will name `codex exec "<prompt>"` as the Codex form of a headless line, whose Claude Code and Antigravity form is `-p "/cairn:<skill>"`. Codex's documented explicit invocation is the `$` sigil, which a shell expands as a variable inside double quotes, and whether Codex accepts `/cairn:<skill>` is unconfirmed. What prompt text, in what quoting, does the page give for invoking a cairn skill through `codex exec`?

The build script gains a new operation (named wording slots in `core/` filled from a new per-host settings key), and no test under `tests/` covers `scripts/build_hosts.py` today; the only checks are the build's own validation gate, `--check`, and the byte-identity diff of the two existing host trees. Does this milestone add automated tests for the new slot operation, and if so, covering what?

The live Codex verification (plugin install, one inline skill, one dispatch of each agent) can be run headless through `codex exec` with the approval-and-sandbox bypass, or as an interactive session under the workspace-write sandbox that the Codex instructions describe to users, where every git staging and commit step asks for approval. In which mode is the live verification run, and is it carried out by the task runner or by the maintainer by hand?

Several recorded decisions rest on Codex behaviour that is still unverified (that `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` reaches the commands a skill runs, that a generic subagent can be spawned and told to read a plugin file, that the marketplace layout installs), and the no-model probes and the live run that would confirm them happen after those decisions were recorded. When a probe or the live verification contradicts a recorded decision, how does the milestone proceed?
